risks.title: Persistent Inflationary Pressures
risks.summary: While inflation is expected to fall, US inflation is projected to return to target more gradually than anticipated, with core PCE inflation remaining elevated. This persistence could necessitate continued tight monetary policy.
risks.watch_for: Core PCE inflation readings above 3% and any signs of unmooring inflation expectations.
sources: Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midyear Outlook Report, June 2026)
Guggenheim Investments (September Economic Outlook and Key Themes, September 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)

risks.title: Geopolitical Tensions and Conflict Escalation
risks.summary: The ongoing conflict in the Middle East continues to drive energy price increases, renewed inflation, and expectations of tighter monetary policy. Escalation of hostilities poses a significant downside risk to global growth and stability.
risks.watch_for: Further escalation of the Middle East conflict, and its impact on energy markets and global trade routes.
sources: Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midyear Outlook Report, June 2026)

risks.title: Elevated US Fiscal Deficits and Rising Debt
risks.summary: The US faces large and growing budget deficits, with debt projected to rise significantly as a percentage of GDP. This trajectory raises concerns about long-term fiscal sustainability and could constrain future policy options.
risks.watch_for: The CBO's updated projections on deficits and debt, and any legislative actions aimed at fiscal consolidation.
sources: Congressional Budget Office (Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036, February 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)

risks.title: Monetary Policy Tightening and Interest Rate Uncertainty
risks.summary: The Federal Reserve has continued to raise interest rates to combat inflation. Uncertainty remains regarding the future path of monetary policy, with potential for further hikes or a prolonged period of higher rates impacting economic activity.
risks.watch_for: FOMC statements, Summary of Economic Projections (SEP), and Fed officials' speeches for signals on future rate decisions.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (June 2026 Economic Outlook and Key Themes)
Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midyear Outlook Report, June 2026)

risks.title: Slowing Global Growth Amidst Divergent Economic Paths
risks.summary: Global growth is projected to slow in 2026, with emerging market and developing economies facing particular challenges. While AI adoption offers some upside, the overall outlook is tempered by geopolitical risks and trade policy uncertainty.
risks.watch_for: Updates to global GDP growth forecasts from the IMF and World Bank, and indicators of trade activity.

risks.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Investment and Economic Impact
risks.summary: AI is a significant driver of business investment and economic growth, particularly in the US. However, there is uncertainty about the full extent of its productivity gains and potential disruptions to the labor market.
risks.watch_for: Corporate investment plans in AI, productivity growth data, and labor market adjustments related to AI adoption.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (September Economic Outlook and Key Themes, September 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)

risks.title: Trade Policy Uncertainty and Tariffs
risks.summary: Ongoing trade policy uncertainty and the potential for higher tariffs continue to pose risks to global trade and economic growth. While some tariffs may have receded, their impact on supply chains and prices persists.
risks.watch_for: Announcements of new tariffs or trade disputes, and their impact on import/export data.
sources: Congressional Budget Office (Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036, February 2026)

risks.title: Labor Market Resilience Amidst Shifting Dynamics
risks.summary: The US labor market has shown resilience with stable unemployment rates and solid job gains. However, concerns remain about the impact of AI and potential shifts in labor supply, which could influence wage growth and employment levels.
risks.watch_for: Monthly jobs reports (nonfarm payrolls), unemployment rate figures, and wage growth data.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)
Guggenheim Investments (September Economic Outlook and Key Themes, September 2026)

consensus_note: There is a broad consensus among institutions regarding the persistent nature of inflation and the significant downside risks posed by geopolitical tensions, particularly the conflict in the Middle East. While AI is seen as a driver of growth, its ultimate impact remains a two-sided risk. Institutions like the CBO highlight concerns about fiscal sustainability due to rising deficits and debt.
